vectors.desc: STRUCT descriptor, name-sorted field table, hash-consed repeat type-ref
deriv: kind 0 STRUCT rides the inline selector D0 (kinds 0..7 inline, 8..15 as D8 u8 — minimality, WF-22 :598-608); body ARG n=2, then pairs {field name, type-ref} in canonical name-sorted order x < y (WF-22 :668-674)
the second field's type-ref is REF d2 — structural identity: two descriptors with the same kind, arguments, and child type-refs are one intern record, the second occurrence a REF (WF-22 :657-660)
value: STRUCT b0, field values in table order — zz(2)=4 (24), zz(1)=2 (22); no per-field tags (WF-19 :541-546)

vectors.desc: NAMED wrapper with Name[args] wire name; wrapper and base intern independently
deriv: kind 6 NAMED, inline D6; the name position exists exactly for the nominal kinds — VARIANT, NAMED, CODER; structural kinds omit it (WF-22 :608, :633-641)
wire name 'Box[int64]' — the Name[args] grammar: constructor name plus bracketed argument list, the arguments canonical structural names (VS-25; WF-22 :641-646)

the wrapper and its base intern independently — nominal names do not participate in the structural key: one structural record per structure, one wrapper per name (WF-22 :657-663); value zz(7)=14 -> 28 0E under the base width (WF-8 :328-331)
the width-8 argument rides the u8 rung 08 08 — the inline rung caps at 7; width 16 is 08 10 (WF-22 :635-639)
the name length 10 exceeds the inline cap 7 — u8 rung 68 0A; a nibble may not carry 8..15 as a value (WF-7 :286-287)

vectors.desc: width argument minimality: INT-16 rides the u8 rung 08 10
deriv: kind 10 INT rides the u8 form D8 0A; the width is one WF-7 argument: 0 = arb (the INT rung only, no fixed width), 1/2/4/8 the machine widths as inline selectors, 16 the u8 form 08 10 — the inline rung caps at 7 (WF-22 :622, :627-631)
value zz(1)=2 (22) fits the 16-wide domain; the width is part of the descriptor's structure (WF-8 :328-331; WF-22 :627-631)

vectors.desc: u8-form kind rung: STRING kind D8 0D, empty body
deriv: kind 13 STRING: selector D8 0D, body empty — as are BOOL (D8 09), BLOB (D8 0E), INTERFACE (D8 08); kinds 8..15 ride the u8 form and no kind that fits the inline rung rides it (WF-22 :598-608, table :610-616)
value STRING 'hi' = 62 68 69 — token 6, ARG len 2, raw bytes; the literal interns id 1 in the unified space (WF-13 :411-423; WF-24 :752)

vectors.desc: ARRAY kind D4: ARG N plus one element type-ref, never duplicated inside the record
deriv: kind 4 ARRAY ([N]T): inline D4, body ARG N = 3, then exactly one type-ref — the element type is never duplicated inside the record; the descriptor context fixes it (WF-22 :606, :610-616, :686-688)
the u8 kind byte 10 reads as kind 16 — kinds 16..255 are reserved and unknown kinds are a format error; the prefix halts at the kind byte (WF-22 :602-604)

vectors.desc: selector non-minimal: inline-capable kind 2 riding the D8 form
deriv: D8 02: kind 2 (TUPLE) fits the inline rung D0..D7 — the kind selector is subject to minimality and no kind that fits the inline rung rides the u8 form (WF-22 :604-608)
canonical spelling opens e0 d2 (V-77's descriptor); one legal selector per kind

vectors.desc: hybrid collision: two distinct nominal types deriving one qualified name
deriv: two NAMED descriptors both derive the qualified name 'T' (first: 61 54 literal, interning id 1; second: name position REF d1) with distinct bases INT-8 and BOOL — one qualified name maps to exactly one descriptor per stream (WF-22 :633-641)

the name policy is hybrid: derived names stay clean, no renaming, no disambiguation suffixes — the encoder rejects at registry start naming both origins, the decode-side counterpart is this format error at the colliding descriptor; the resolution is explicit name binding (VS-10; WF-22 :645-651)

vectors.desc: std.decimal reserved: rebinding the standard namespace rejected
deriv: a NAMED descriptor deriving 'std.decimal' over an INT-8 base: the reserved standard namespace cannot collide with a language-derived name — std.decimal names the decimal interchange composition (unscaled INT-arb, scale INT-32) and a binding may not rebind it (WF-22 :651-653; WF-11 :393-397)
a name bound to two different types, or a binding conflicting with a reserved standard name, rejects with an unsupported-type error — the decode-side class is the binding conflict (WF-22 :684-687)
the name 'std.decimal' is 11 bytes — 7374642e646563696d616c on the u8 length rung 68 0B (WF-7 :286-287; WF-22 :717)

vectors.desc: custom coder body unskippable: decode without the registration
deriv: kind 15 CODER: D8 0F, nominal name 'cx' (62 63 78), ARG coderTag 1, body 2A defined by the coder registered for the name; the tag binds 1:1 to the name per stream (WF-22 :610-616, :682-685); the value body 2B is the coder's own encoding

a decoder without that registration cannot step over the body — its length is not derivable from the grammar; bodies of user-registered coders stay unskippable and reject with an unsupported-type error, never a silent skip (WF-6 :261, :273-274); would-be canonical bytes under the registered encoder

vectors.desc: TUPLE-typed root, value token 51 — nonzero reserved low nibble
deriv: envelope: root DESC TUPLE E0 D2 with arity ARG 00 — zero elements (WF-22 :621, :692-693); the value position is known and TUPLE-typed, the token 51

for the FLOAT, TUPLE, STRUCT, and DESC value tokens (40, 50, B0, E0) the low nibble is reserved — a decoder MUST reject a nonzero nibble (WF-23 :772-775); an unknown opcode — any selector or form not defined for its class and position — in a known position is a format error, silent skipping forbidden (:777-779)
not a BOOL-selector case: the position is TUPLE-typed and the token is class 5, so the BOOL row's enumerated selectors (:745) never apply — V-40 keeps the BOOL-selector class on its own bytes

vectors.desc: root byte-slice position whose desc spells SLICE-of-UINT-8 where BLOB is the canonical grain
deriv: the root type is a byte slice, whose canonical kind is BLOB — the canonical byte-sequence kind: a byte slice encoded as a SLICE of UINT-8 is non-canonical (WF-22 :700-701)

the desc spells the violation itself — E0 D3 (SLICE) over E0 D8 0B 01 (UINT-8) — and canonical mode is always on, a decode-side contract: a SLICE of UINT-8 in a byte-slice position is a decoder reject, not an encoder convention (WF-25 :967-973); the prefix halts at the desc, no value body can follow legally
